text.en: Meena's uncle grew a high-yielding rice variety. "Plant breeding did this," he said.

The Green Revolution increased food grain production in many places through changes that included new crop varieties, irrigation and fertilisers. Crop improvement uses inherited variation and evaluates traits such as harvest reliability and food quality in context. Selection and hybridisation are examples of conventional breeding.
Animal breeding considers inherited traits, genetic diversity and animal welfare. A hybrid may show stronger performance for some traits, known as heterosis, but results depend on the trait and the environment.
Biotechnology uses living systems, organisms or their products in useful applications. Examples include food fermentation and medicines such as insulin. Genetic engineering directly changes genetic material, and stem cells can give rise to specialised cells. DNA profiles can support comparisons for identity. Benefits, risks, fairness, animal welfare and access should be considered before applying these technologies.
The Green Revolution raised food grain production using high-yielding varieties, fertilisers and irrigation.

board.text: Green Revolution

text.en: Plant breeding uses inherited variation to develop crop varieties. The chapter compares selection and hybridisation with other broad categories of crop improvement.

board.text: hybridisation

text.en: Crop improvement can aim for reliable harvests, food quality, or suitable performance in local growing conditions. Different communities may value different traits.

board.text: heterosis

text.en: Animal breeding includes inbreeding, which mates closely related animals, outbreeding, which mates unrelated ones, and heterosis, the extra vigour of hybrids.

board.text: genetic engineering

text.en: Genetic engineering is a group of approaches that change genetic material directly. This differs from conventional breeding, which works with inherited variation across generations.

board.text: stem cells

text.en: Biotechnology has uses in food, agriculture and medicine. Some stem cells can produce specialised cells. DNA profiles can help compare biological samples, and genetic modification can involve different kinds of change.

board.text: DNA fingerprinting

text.en: Individuals in a population can differ in visible features. Conventional breeding works with differences that can pass to offspring.

board.text: Breeding draws on inherited variation

text.en: Two plants of the same variety may grow differently if one has less water. A visible difference alone does not prove an inherited difference.

board.text: Environment can change how a trait appears

text.en: If people prefer a certain inherited feature, the plants or animals in later generations can contain a different mix of traits.

board.text: Selection changes which variants are represented

text.en: In a conventional breeding example, offspring can inherit features associated with both parents. Inheritance does not guarantee a perfect combination.

board.text: A hybrid has parents from different varieties

text.en: A hybrid may perform better for one trait than its parents did. That effect is called heterosis, or hybrid vigour.

board.text: Heterosis concerns a measured trait

text.en: A variety may do well in one growing season and poorly in another. Compare the conditions before generalising from one observation.

board.text: An advantage can depend on conditions

text.en: Food grain production rose in many areas with new varieties, improved water supply, fertiliser and other changes in farming.

board.text: The Green Revolution involved several changes

text.en: More grain can improve food supply. Water use, fertiliser costs and access to resources can also affect farmers and communities.

board.text: The benefits and costs can differ by place

text.en: Taste, nutrition, storage and harvest reliability can matter as much as the total weight produced.

board.text: Yield is one of several useful measures

text.en: Different varieties preserve different inherited features. This can give communities more options when weather or local needs change.

board.text: Genetic diversity offers more than one option

text.en: A feature useful to people does not automatically improve an animal’s health. A decision should consider how the animals live as well as production.

board.text: Animal breeding includes welfare considerations

text.en: Closely related parents are more likely to share some inherited variants. That can raise the chance of offspring inheriting two copies of a harmful recessive allele.

board.text: Inbreeding involves related parents

text.en: It can increase the variety of alleles in offspring. Its effect depends on the animals and the traits being studied.

board.text: Outbreeding involves less closely related parents

text.en: The word covers long-established uses and newer applications. Making curd with helpful microorganisms is a familiar example.

board.text: Biotechnology uses living systems or their products

text.en: Microorganisms transform substances already present in some foods. The result can change texture, flavour and keeping qualities.

board.text: Fermentation is an established use

text.en: Conventional breeding works through inheritance across generations. Genetic engineering changes genetic material more directly. These are categories to compare, each with different possible uses.

board.text: Genetic engineering and conventional breeding differ

text.en: Insulin made for medical use is an example of biotechnology producing a useful biological product. Its purpose is to help manage blood glucose under healthcare guidance.

board.text: Some medicines can be made with biotechnology

text.en: Stem cells can renew themselves, and some can give rise to specialised cell types. Their potential depends on the type of stem cell.

board.text: Stem cells have two important properties

text.en: A laboratory finding can be a reason to study a possible use. It does not by itself show that a treatment is safe and effective.

board.text: Established treatments differ from research possibilities

text.en: Specialists can compare profiles to see how closely biological samples match. A conclusion also depends on the quality of the evidence.

board.text: A DNA profile is a comparison tool

text.en: Genetic information can be sensitive and may also relate to relatives. Consent and careful handling matter when such information is collected or used.

board.text: DNA data deserve privacy

text.en: Ask what was measured, who might benefit, and what trade-offs are possible. A fair comparison also states when evidence is uncertain.

board.text: A useful claim still needs evidence

text.en: Food production, animal welfare, and human healthcare raise different questions. Good decisions consider evidence and the people or living systems affected.

board.text: Different applications call for different questions

text.en: One crop can score well on yield while another needs less water. State the goal and compare the relevant traits before making a judgement.

board.text: Compare options before deciding what better means

text.en: Hybridisation crosses two varieties.
The offspring combine their traits.
The offspring is a hybrid.

problem.en: Two crop varieties produce similar harvests, but one needs less irrigation. Which should a water-limited community consider?

text.en: Compare how much water each option needs for a similar harvest.

why.en: The local constraint is limited water, so the trait matters.

text.en: Consider the lower-water option along with costs and other evidence.

why.en: A decision depends on several measures, including local conditions.

problem.en: Why does a plant’s size alone not reveal whether it inherited a tendency to be tall?

text.en: Plant size can respond to water, light and nutrients.

why.en: Conditions influence how inherited differences appear.

text.en: A single observation cannot distinguish inheritance from environment.

why.en: Use other evidence before interpreting what caused the size difference.

problem.en: A news report describes a promising stem-cell finding. Does it show that a treatment is ready for use?

text.en: Promising evidence raises a question that needs more study.

why.en: Research results do not automatically establish effectiveness in people.

text.en: Evidence about benefits and safety is needed before use is justified.

why.en: Distinguish an application being studied from a treatment already established.

prompt.en: A friend says DNA fingerprinting is used to cook food. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: It is used in crime and parentage tests.

points.en: Crop breeding uses inherited variation to develop varieties for particular needs.
Heterosis means improved hybrid performance for a particular trait.
Some stem cells can produce specialised cells.
